objective: Add GeekHunter and Nerdin as independently verified public job sources to the existing canary catalog, preserving their real job descriptions, publication timestamps and eligibility metadata.
allowed_changes: Register exactly two public source adapters, GeekHunter and Nerdin, in the existing catalog and source selector
Read bounded public listing and per-job JobPosting structured metadata with existing HTTP and parser facilities
Keep genuine source dates, description, salary, company, location, work mode, eligibility and direct URLs when published
Deduplicate by URL, classify with unchanged existing filters and expose honest per-source failures
Add failing-then-passing tests and publish the validated update only on the isolated existing canary
forbidden_changes: main or operational Render service, production Neon, history, candidate applications or authentication
new scheduler, database schema, parallel search engine, paid API, external credential, new dependency or paid service
scraping behind login, bypassing anti-bot protection, guessing unavailable job fields or automatic applications
CV engine, ranking formulas, existing providers, unrelated frontend redesign, GitHub Actions or Vercel
acceptance: Both official public sources are represented in source filters and catalog tasks
A reproducible real posting from each provider retains verified JD, date and source URL
Missing data remains unconfirmed and source errors cannot masquerade as zero available jobs
Scoped regression tests and build pass, with before-after evidence and no change to main
Existing isolated canary deploy is live and its UI bundle exposes the new providers for human homologation
deployment: Use existing source fidelity canary and isolated Neon branch; no main merge without express approval
